chunks: And by this chain, he said:

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said to his companions: Believe in Laylat al-Qadr, for it shall be for ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, and for his eleven descendants after me.

key_terms.الْأَحَدَ عَشَرَ: the eleven, referring to the eleven Imams after Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْقَدْرِ: the divine decree or determination, referring here to Laylat al-Qadr
key_terms.لِعَلِيِّ: for ʿAlī, indicating his special connection to the matter mentioned
key_terms.مِنْ بَعْدِي: after me, indicating succession following the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith connect Laylat al-Qadr to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام and the eleven Imams after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Laylat al-Qadr in connection with the authority and station of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام and the eleven Imams from his descendants after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. In Shia doctrine, it indicates the continuing divine matter and religious authority vested in the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali: ‘He (Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>) said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> to his<sup>saww</sup> companions: ‘Believe in the Night of Pre-determination (لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ), it would occur for Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> and for his<sup>asws</sup> sons<sup>asws</sup>, the eleven from after me<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 12. Through same chain of narrators the following is narrated.
“the Messenger of Allah once said to his companions, ‘You must believ in the Layla al-Qadr (night of destiny). It is Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) and his eleven descendants after me.”
